title: Establish a Cloud-First Policy for New Application Development
narrative: FEDC's application portfolio is split between on-premise infrastructure and cloud-hosted services, with no consistent policy governing where new applications are deployed. This has resulted in a fragmented operational model, with separate teams managing on-premise and cloud infrastructure, inconsistent security postures, and missed opportunities for elasticity and managed services. We establish a cloud-first policy: all new application capabilities must be designed and deployed on cloud infrastructure by default. On-premise deployment requires a formal architectural exception approved by the architecture review board, with documented justification covering data sovereignty, latency, or regulatory constraints. Existing on-premise applications will be assessed for migration as part of the annual portfolio review.

requirements.title: Cloud-native design requirement
requirements.description: All new applications must be designed as cloud-native, using containerisation, managed databases, and cloud-native scaling patterns where available.

requirements.title: Exception process
requirements.description: Any deviation from cloud-first deployment must follow the architectural exception process and be reviewed and approved by the architecture review board before development begins.

requirements.title: Security baseline
requirements.description: All cloud-hosted applications must comply with the FEDC cloud security baseline, including identity federation, encryption at rest and in transit, and automated vulnerability scanning.
